title: Isandro and the Border
premise: Dominic Quintana, a sleepless interpreter haunted by a massacre he witnessed and translated away, is attached to a doomed trilateral peace delegation at the San Isandro border crossing. When a dead colleague's voiceprint unlocks a hidden server, Dominic finds recordings proving the massacre was ordered, not accidental—and that the assassin sent to bury the evidence is the woman he once loved. To survive, he must smuggle the truth past three governments, outmaneuver his handlers, and choose between the justice the law forbids and the duty that protects him, ending at the checkpoint itself where he trades his immunity for the recordings' release and walks across the border as a nameless man, finally able to sleep.
about_author: O. M. Almeida is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind the glass of diplomatic summits before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about the people who translate other people's lies.

chapters.title: Third Shift Silence
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Opening at the San Isandro checkpoint during night shift, we meet a man surviving on four hours of sleep, translating pleasantries for a peace delegation he privately believes is theater. A flashback fragment of the massacre surfaces mid-interpretation, and he mistranslates a single word to keep the talks alive. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Sorting the effects of his dead colleague Marisol, Dominic finds a voice-locked drive; on impulse he speaks her name-phrase and a server in Lisbon unlocks, streaming audio files. He recognizes his own translated voice on one recording—edited to sound like consent. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering his invisibility was engineered.

chapters.title: Three Flags, One Room
chapters.summary: Delegation POV, alternating between the three chief negotiators. The talks stall over a border demarcation neither side will sign, and each government quietly tasks its security attaché with controlling information flow. Dominic realizes all three want the same thing: silence. Emotional beat: dread as the room's civility reveals itself as a cage.

chapters.title: What Marisol Recorded
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Decoding the files over two sleepless nights, Dominic maps the massacre's true chain of command—a colonel, a minister, a signature. The final file is a video message Marisol made for him, naming a courier route through the checkpoint's freight lane. Emotional beat: grief converting into purpose.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Wire
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Introduced as the assassin contracted to retrieve and destroy the server, Elena Vargas works the delegation's perimeter with cold efficiency—until she identifies the voiceprint's new owner as Dominic, the man she loved before the war made them instruments. Emotional beat: love and duty drawing a knife-edge line through her.

chapters.title: Dead Drop at Kilometer Nine
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Following Marisol's courier route, Dominic copies the archive onto analog tape and hides copies in three places only he would think to look. His handler, Serrano, grows suspicious and schedules Dominic for 'repatriation'—a euphemism. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Interrogation in the Blue Room
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Dominic and Elena. Elena corners Dominic in the delegation's blue room, gun drawn, and instead of killing him demands to hear one file. Listening together, they confirm her own government ordered the massacre. She lets him live, and both know the clock is now running. Emotional beat: betrayal of country becoming loyalty to each other.

chapters.title: The Checkpoint Shifts
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with intercut Serrano chapters. The border checkpoint changes shift schedules—Marisol's warning—and the freight-lane window closes in twelve hours. Serrano detains Dominic, offering immunity for the tapes; Dominic pretends to bargain while Elena, off the grid, disables the compound's communications. Emotional beat: the trap tightening, courage hardening.

chapters.title: Everything Past the Glass
chapters.summary: Dominic and Elena's alternating POV. Climax: Dominic broadcasts the recordings live into the negotiation chamber through the interpretation system itself, forcing all three delegations to hear the truth in their own languages. Serrano orders him shot; Elena takes the bullet meant for him, and Dominic, bleeding, finishes the translation. Emotional beat: love against duty, resolved at the cost of everything.

chapters.title: The Man Who Slept
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, weeks later. The colonel is indicted, the talks collapse into something more honest, and Dominic—stripped of rank and immunity—crosses the San Isandro border as an ordinary traveler with no documents worth seizing. In a cheap hotel on the far side, he sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, and peace inside it.
